# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 75 (Bu-Vb Pc75)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc75
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 75
**Title (English, from literature):** Raising a hand in anger
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bu-vb-pc75
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Talasattika-sikkhāpada* ("Training rule on raising a hand in anger"), designated as Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 75 in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka, prohibits a Buddhist monk from physically threatening or gesturing violently against another monk out of anger [SuttaCentral]. According to the rule's summary definition, a bhikkhu who gives into anger and makes a threatening gesture with a raised hand or palm toward another monk incurs an offense requiring formal confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. Shayne Clarke notes the rule in passing in a comparative enumeration of Vinaya prātimokṣa rules alongside its corresponding bhikkhunī counterpart [Clarke, Pārājika]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate wide transmission of this rule across almost all early Buddhist Vinaya traditions [SuttaCentral]. Corresponding rules exist in the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Pc 75), *Bhikkhu Parivāra* (Pc 75), *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Pc 153), and *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pc 153) [SuttaCentral]. External parallels survive in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan Vinaya texts across multiple monastic lineages, including the Sarvāstivāda (Chinese Pc 49; Sanskrit Prātimokṣa Pc 49), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit Pc 49), Mahīśāsaka (Chinese Pc 72), Dharmaguptaka (Chinese Pc 79), and Mahāsāṅghika/Lokottaravāda (Chinese and Sanskrit Pc 59), alongside corresponding nuns' rules in these schools [SuttaCentral].
Computational text-reuse data generated by DharmaNexus corroborate significant shared formulary within the Pali Vinaya, showing substantial reuse particularly with adjacent rules in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*, such as Pācittiya 74, 76, 77, and 78 [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments in DharmaNexus link this rule to Tibetan Vinaya texts, including the Mūlasarvāstivāda *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3) as well as the commentaries *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104) and *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2), matching the Tibetan parallels recognized by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
